The bug is in `middleware/auth.js:23`. Token expiry uses `currentTime > token.expiry`, which keeps tokens valid *at* the exact expiry time. At the boundary, `currentTime == expiry`, so the token isn't rejected.

Fix: change `>` to `>=`:

```javascript
if (currentTime >= token.expiry) {
  return reject('Token expired');
}
```

This rejects tokens when current time reaches or exceeds expiry, which is the correct behavior—a token shouldn't be usable at its exact expiration moment.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="Edit">
<parameter name="path">middleware/auth.js</parameter>
<parameter name="oldText">  if (currentTime > token.expiry) {
    return reject('Token expired');</parameter>
<parameter name="newText">  if (currentTime >= token.expiry) {
    return reject('Token expired');</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Done. Tokens now correctly reject at the exact expiry boundary instead of one millisecond after.
